delivery-returns.title: Delivery and returns
content: Free delivery on orders over $80, usually in 2–3 working days. Order before 3 pm on a weekday and it leaves the same day.
You have 30 days to send it back for a full refund. Print the label from your account and drop the parcel at any post office.
Laptops and phones have a 2-year warranty; everything else has one year. If it goes wrong, we collect it, fix it and bring it back.

choose-a-laptop-for-study.title: How to choose a laptop for study
choose-a-laptop-for-study.excerpt: Weight, battery, screen and memory: what matters for four years of lectures and essays, and what doesn’t.
content: A laptop for study gets carried more than any other. It goes to every lecture, the library and home for the holidays, so weight and battery matter more than raw speed.
Under 1.3 kg is light enough that you won’t notice it in a bag. Look for at least 12 hours of battery, so you can leave the charger at home for a full day.
A 13″ or 14″ screen is the sweet spot: big enough for two documents side by side, small enough for a library desk. A sharper screen (2.5K or more) is easier on the eyes for long reading.
8 GB is enough for essays, browsing and video calls.
16 GB is worth it for design, coding or lots of tabs.
256 GB of storage fills up fast with photos: 512 GB if you can.
A gaming graphics card, a 4K screen and a huge drive. They add weight and cost, and they drain the battery.

noise-cancelling-explained.title: Noise cancelling, explained
noise-cancelling-explained.excerpt: What noise cancelling does, what it can’t do, and whether it’s worth paying more for.
content: Noise cancelling headphones listen to the sound around you and play the opposite wave, so the two cancel out before they reach your ear.
Steady, low sounds: train and plane engines, air conditioning, the hum of an office. These almost disappear.
Sudden or high sounds, like voices or a dog barking, get quieter but don’t go away. A good fit around the ear does as much for those as the electronics.
Over-ears cancel more and last longer. Earbuds go in a pocket. If you commute and sit at a desk, many people end up with both.

smart-bulbs-where-to-start.title: Smart bulbs: where to start
smart-bulbs-where-to-start.excerpt: Start with two bulbs and one routine. Here’s which, and why.
content: The easiest way into a smart home is a smart bulb. It fits the lamp you already have, and you can set it up in five minutes from your phone.
Put one in the lamp you use most in the evening and one by your bed. That’s where a schedule makes the biggest difference.
Bedside light on slowly, ten minutes before your alarm.
Living room down to warm and dim at 9 pm.
Everything off when the last phone leaves home.
Not for Wi-Fi bulbs. A hub helps once you have more than twenty devices, or want them to work when the internet is down.
